PREVIOUSLISTINGATTEMPT
In view of the growing potential of stock market in the PRC, our Company entered into a
tutoring agreement (輔導協議) with China Merchants Securities Co., Ltd. (招商證券股份有限公
司)(“CMS”) onDecember 2,2020inpreparationfortheAsharelistingapplicationontheScienceand
Technology Innovation Board of Shanghai Stock Exchange (上海證券交易所科創板) and made a
preliminary filing (上市輔導備案) with the Beijing office of the CSRC on December 18, 2020. We
voluntarily withdrew from our A-share listing preparation after a comprehensive assessment taking
intoaccounttheuncertaintyofthetimetableofourCompany’sA-sharelistingprocess,thethenmarket
circumstancesandourthendevelopmentstrategiesinwhichwehavedecidedtofocusourresourceson
the research and development of 51Earth and optimization and business development of 51Aes and
51Sim,WeterminatedourengagementwithChinaMerchantsSecuritiesCo.,Ltd.onAugust25,2022.
We have not submitted any listing application to the regulatory authorities for our previous attempt
withtheShanghaiStockExchange.
We commenced our A-share listing preparation in December 2023 following our then
re-assessment ofthethenpolicyandmarketcircumstances.Weenteredintoatutoringagreement(輔導
協議) with Kaiyuan Securities Co., Ltd. (開源證券股份有限公司) (“Kaiyuan”) on December 21, 2023
in preparation for the A share listing application on the Beijing Stock Exchange (北京證券交易所) and
we made a preliminary filing with the Beijing office of the CSRC on December 26, 2023. We have
selected Kaiyuan for the tutoring agreement and our preparation for our A-share listing on the Beijing
Stock Exchange because Kaiyuan had rich experience in capital market transactions on the National
EquitiesExchangeandQuotations,thepredecessoroftheBeijingStockExchange.
After the first half of 2024, we re-assessed our A-share listing preparation, the then listing
policies and environment in the PRC and elsewhere and continued to explore other market
opportunities. With the promulgation of Chapter 18C of the Listing Rules in March 2023 and the
listing of the first listing applicant under Chapter 18C of the Listing Rules in June 2024, we saw the
opportunity for us, being a specialist technology company, to achieve listing status on the Stock
Exchange,whichwouldbebeneficialtoourCompanyandShareholdersinthattheStockExchange,as
aleadingplayeroftheinternationalfinancialmarkets,couldofferusadirectaccesstotheinternational
capital markets, thereby enhancing our fund-raising capabilities and broadening our fund-raising
channels and our Shareholders base as well as strengthening our international exposure. Specifically,
the Company having taken into account the following factors decided to pursue a listing on the Stock
Exchangeasa18Cspecialisttechnologycompany:
(cid:129) the Stock Exchange, as a leading player of the international financial markets, could offer
the Company a direct access to the international capital markets, enhance its fundraising
capabilities and broaden its fundraising channels and its Shareholders base as well as
strengthenitscorporategovernance;
(cid:129) the promulgation of Chapter 18C of the ListingRules inMarch 2023and the listingofthe
first listing applicant under Chapter 18C of the Listing Rules in June 2024, which the
Company considers a prime opportunity for the Company to attain a listing status on a
recognizedstockexchange;

Publicfloat
Our Company has applied for H-share full circulation and the CSRC issued notice of filing on
November 24,2025forthe conversion of363,299,144UnlistedSharesintoHSharesupontheListing.
Upon completion of the Global Offering and the conversion of certain Unlisted Shares into H Shares,
the 19,081,808 Unlisted Shares held by the existing Shareholders, representing approximately 4.7% of
our total issued Shares uponthe Global Offering(assuming the Over-allotmentOptionis notexercised
and the share options granted under our Pre-IPO Share Option Scheme are not exercised), will not be
considered as part of the public float as these Unlisted Shares will not be converted into H Shares and
willnotbelisteduponthecompletionoftheGlobalOffering.
In addition, upon completion of the Global Offering and conversion of certain Unlisted Shares
into H Shares, 66,209,905, 32,618,800 and 42,903,742 H Shares are to be held by LS 51World (a
substantial shareholder of our Company), Starcraft Technology (a company controlled by Mr. Li, our
executive Director and substantial shareholder) and Mr. Li (our executive Director and substantial
shareholder), respectively. These entities, which constitute the core connected persons of our
Company, will, in aggregate, hold 141,732,447 H Shares, representing approximately 34.9% of our
total issued Shares upon the completion of the Global Offering. These shares will not be counted
towards the public float. Accordingly, the 19,081,808 Unlisted Shares and 141,732,447 H Shares, in
aggregate, representing 39.6% of our total issued Shares upon the completion of the Global Offering
(assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised and the share options granted under our Pre-IPO
ShareOptionSchemearenotexercised),willnotbecountedtowardsthepublicfloat.
Save as disclosed above, upon the completion of the Global Offering and the conversion of
certain Unlisted Shares into H Shares, 221,566,697 H Shares to be held by our Shareholders who are
not our core connected persons, representing approximately 54.5% of our total issued Shares upon the
completion of the Global Offering (assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not exercised and the
share options granted under our Pre-IPO Share Option Scheme are not exercised), will be counted
towards the public float. Together with the issue of 23,975,200 H Shares pursuant to the Global
Offering(assumingthattheOver-allotmentOptionisnotexercisedandtheshareoptionsgrantedunder
our Pre-IPO Share Option Scheme are not exercised), representing approximately 5.9% of our total
issuedShares,approximately60.4%ofourtotalissuedShareswillbecountedtowardsthepublicfloat.

expected to be over HK$6,000 million but not exceeding HK$30,000 million based on the Offer Price
of HK$30.5 per Offer Share, the minimum prescribed percentage of H Shares held by public at the
time of Listing pursuant to Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules would be the higher of (i) the
percentage that would result in the expected market value of H Shares held by the public to be
HK$1,500,000,000atthetimeofListing;and(ii)15%.
Based on the Offer Price of HK$30.50 and assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not
exercised,thepercentagethatwouldresultintheexpectedmarketvalueofHSharesheldbythepublic
to be HK$1,500,000,000 will be approximately 12.7%. Therefore, pursuant to Rule 19A.13A(1) of the

SatisfactionoftheFreeFloatRequirement
Rule19A.13C(1)oftheListingRulesprovidesthat,whereanewapplicantisaPRCissuerwith
no other listed shares at the time of listing, this will normally mean that the portion of H shares for
which listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any disposal restrictions (whether
under contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or otherwise), at the time of listing, must:
(a) represent at least 10% of the total number of issued shares in the class to which H shares belong at
the time of listing (excluding treasury shares), with an expected market value at the time of listing of
not less than HK$50,000,000; or (b) have an expected market value at the time of listing of not less
thanHK$600,000,000.
Pursuant to the applicable PRC law, within the 12 months following the Listing Date, all
existing Shareholders (including the Pre-IPO Investors) cannot dispose of any of the Shares held by
them.Assuch,HSharesheldbytheexistingShareholdersasofthedateofthisprospectusshallnotbe
counted towards the free float of the H Shares of the Company at the time of Listing. Based on the
Offer Price of HK$30.5 per Offer Share, the Company is expected to satisfy the free float requirement
underRule19A.13C(1)oftheListingRules.

OVERVIEW
AboutUs
We are a digital twin technology company in China. We have developed core competencies in
technologyaroundthreemajorareas:3Dgraphics,simulation,andAI.
We were founded in February 2015. Based on the significant growth in the amount of
information data and the swift advancement of information carriers, our founder observed that real-
time 3D would become the most effective way of information interaction after text, images, and video
andisaninevitableoutcomeofthedevelopmentoftheinformationage.Atthattime,real-time3Dwas
mainly used in the field of games to immerse users in a virtual world of entertainment interaction. In
light of the ongoing advancements in technology and the increasing focus on industrial applications,
we have chosen to expand the scope of our real-time 3D capabilities to a broader field. With our keen
judgment and profound understanding of the industry, we believe creating a digital twin of the Earth
can be broken down into five categories of elements, namely buildings, roads, plants, water, and
terrain, and five stages, namely the static world, the dynamic world, the semi-simulated world, the
fully-simulatedworld,and,thedigitaltwinworld.
Thus far, we have entered the fourthstage ofcreating a digitaltwinofthe Earth,achieved real-
time generation and rendering of the entire Earth (at L1 city-level accuracy) and successfully
commercialized at scale the modeling technology underlying our core businesses that is capable of
generating a city a day, which we have successfully demonstrated by generating a city in a day during
theTrackRecordPeriod.Ourgoalistocompletethefifthstagein2030,withtheaimofbuildinga1:1
digitaltwinscenewiththerealworldtoenhancetheefficiency,safety,andthequalityoftherealworld
by solving real-world problems in areas such as traffic, AI training, spatial and temporal immersion,
security warnings, climate prediction, and energy. In line with our vision, we have set a clear
development path and achieved several milestones through continuous technological breakthroughs,
productiterations,andscenarioextensions:
(cid:129) We are a digital twin technology in China, ranking first in the following key metrics for
technologycompanies,accordingtoFrost&Sullivan:
o We were the first in the digital twin industry to propose and consistently
implementtheEarthCloneProject;
o Werankedfirstintermsofrevenuein2024inthedigitaltwinindustryinChina;

ChinaasofDecember31,2024;

twinindustryinChina;

(cid:129) We have formed three core businesses, namely 51Aes (Digital Twin Platform), 51Sim
(Synthetic Data and Simulation Platform) and 51Earth (Digital Earth Platform), and have
releasedcommercializedproductsandsolutionsinallofthesethreebusinesslines.
(cid:129) We have abundant IP rights and play an active role in shaping domestic and international
standards. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had 265 software copyrights and valid

SecondCurve:51SimSyntheticDataandSimulationPlatform
51Sim, launched in 2017, is a leading synthetic data and simulation platform in China. Its core
products include SimOne, a simulation platform for intelligent driving and robotics, DataOne, a data
closed-loop and synthetic data platform, and TIM, a platform for traffic information modeling.
Utilizing advanced data-driven simulation technology, distributed cloud simulation technology,
end-to-end simulation technology, generative AI technology and other core technologies, 51Sim
provides customers with software products and solutions for intelligent driving simulation testing and
synthetic data used for AI system training. These products help developers better understand the
performance of the intelligent driving system in different scenarios and continuously optimize and
improve the autonomous driving algorithms to improve the safety and performance of the system.
51Sim is a mass-production oriented simulation platform in China, and has already provided
commercialized services to hundreds of customers in the intelligent driving industry. Besides, several
products of 51Sim have pan-industry extensibility, and are intended to build general simulation and
syntheticdataplatformsformoreindustries.
ThirdCurve:51EarthDigitalEarthPlatform
Launched in 2022, 51Earth embodies the history of our brand, technology and product
development with a vision to create a digital twin world that is accessible to and contributable by both
enterprises and consumers. We anticipate that 51Earth will become a platform for delivering digital
experiencesthroughdiverseapplications.Thisplatformaimstobringtogetherbuilders,developersand
consumers,providingthemwithplatforms,productsandeconomicsystems,toengageusersaroundthe
world to participate in the Earth Clone Project and experience diverse application scenarios. Through
thesediverseapplications,westrivetocreatedistinctiveexperiencesforconsumersanddrivesustained
business growth and expansion. While the development and commercialization of 51Earth is a long-
term goal, the platform is currently focusing on laying the groundwork by providing the digital twin
assets required by See3 and Short3A developers while continuing to accumulate data to support its

OurAddressableMarketsAndMarketOpportunities
A digital twin technology is a technology that employs 3D graphics, simulation and AI to
generate a highly accurate, virtual replica of a physical object or a system such as a city building or a
vehicle. The types of data handled by our Group to generate such virtual replica mainly include self-
created data, the data purchased from suppliers, and the data generated by customers using our
products. Self-created data primarily include 3D models generated and accumulated by us through the
years of our operations such as general 3D models of trees, buildings and other daily objects. Data
from suppliers and customers include physical data, energy data, environmental data (water/air/noise),
and traffic data and traffic flow, etc., which include real-time data collected from the physical
environment through sensors and machines. This virtual model can mirror the real-world counterparts
in detail, allowing users to observe, analyze and predict how it behaves and changes over time. Digital
twins are used in various fields to simulate and plan scenarios such as urban development, traffic
management, and emergency response strategies with those impacting the actual environment. The
addressable market of digital twin technologies can be broadly categorized into design and operation
optimization,AItrainingandvalidationanduserinteractionandexperience.
175

=== PAGE 185 ===
BUSINESS
Designandoperationoptimization.
Digital twin technology for design and operation, uses advanced sensors and data transmission
to create a detailed virtual model of physical assets. This model helps in collecting real-time data,
analyzing it with AI and feeding back insights to enhance the performance and efficiency of the
real-world system. For example, in a water conservation facility, digital twins integrate data from
reservoirs and hydrological stations to create a comprehensive model. This model enables flood early
warning systems, optimize water resources, planning and monitors environmental conditions, thereby
improvingthefacilities’operationaleffectivenessandresourcesmanagement.
AItrainingandvalidation
In AI training and validation, digital twins serve as a safe and scalable platform to test and
refine AI algorithms. For example, by simulating real-world conditions such as varying weather
patterns, traffic scenarios, pedestrian behavior and unexpected obstacles. Digital twins create a
comprehensive testing environment that mirrors the complexity of actual driving situations.
Additionally, synthetic data such as diverse road layouts and different vehicle types, can be generated
and a wide range of sensor inputs allows for robust training data sets that covers scenarios not easily
replicable in the real world. This approach helps developers of autonomous vehicles to meet
performancestandardsandensuresafetyandreliabilitybeforerealworlddeployment.

virtual environments that reflect real world settings. It is used across sectors, including traveling,
gaming and education. These solutions meet the growing demand for engaging life-like digital
experience from exploring cities to touring historical landmarks. Digital twins offer users detailed and
dynamic virtual scenarios that are enriched with interactions with both cultural and educational
context.

EntryBarriersofOurIndustry
Technology andData:Traditionalinformationinteractionmethodsareinsufficienttomeetthe
evolving needs of enterprises and consumers for information carriers and delivery quality. Digital
twins have emerged as a crucial avenue for advancing the digital economy and facilitating the digital
transformation of enterprises. The development of digital twins demands sophisticated technology,
robust engineering capabilities, and advanced data access, presenting significant barriers to entry.
Consequently, customers prefer to collaborate with companies that possess leading technologies and
superior data acquisition and processing capabilities to achieve efficient upgrades and secure a first-
moveradvantage.
Talent and Ecosystem: The digital twin industry encompasses a wide array of complex
application scenarios and objectives, necessitating in-depth research and the cultivation of diverse
industry segments to create comprehensive, user-friendly, and highly scalable solutions. Thus, it is
imperative to recruit interdisciplinary and composite background talents while enhancing technical
investments. Additionally, ecological linkage is a vital industry barrier. By establishing platforms to
build ecosystems and enable data integration, system integration, multi-party collaboration, and
continuous innovation, we can connect with multiple ecological partners to achieve long-term
sustainabledevelopment.

OURSTRATEGIES
Our overarching strategy, vision, and mission are centered around creating digital version of
Earth’s 510 million square kilometers. This ambitious endeavor aims to enhance the efficiency, safety,
and quality of the real world. Our strategy unfolds in five progressive stages: the static world, the
dynamic world, the semi-simulated world, the fully-simulated world, and finally, the complete digital
twin earth. We aim to further solidify and enhance our industry leadership through relentless
innovationandimprovement.
We recognize three majorchallenges inthe digitaltwinindustry:data standards, creation costs,
and application value. Moving forward, to achieve the fourth stage of our strategy, we will iterate and
enhance our products around digital infrastructure, AI synthetic data, digital earth ecosystem
development,andcommercialexpansion,withaparticularfocusonestablishinganoverseasmarketing
networkandateamofskilledprofessionals.Thedetailsofourstrategyareasfollows:
EmpowerDigitalInfrastructurethrough51Aes
Inthefuture,the51AesplatformwillintegratethefivecorecompetenciesofProposal(efficient
evaluation and comparison), Planning (intelligent planning and deduction), Promotion (precise
investment promotion and sales), Project (green building and construction), and Program (safe
operation andmanagement),allofwhichwillbebuiltonaunifiedurbandatabase,tofurtherdevelopa
city digital infrastructure. Specifically, 51Aes platform’s five core competencies work in synergy to
transform urban development. In terms of Proposals, the platform enables efficient evaluation of
design proposals byintegratingthemwithreal-worldelementssuchasterrain,waterways, andexisting
infrastructure,makingdesignproposalsmorerealisticandintuitive.IntermsofPlanning,itsintelligent
deduction capabilities leverage comprehensive data on land use, population, and traffic flows to
simulate and optimize development scenarios, ensuring plans align with both current conditions and
181

=== PAGE 191 ===
BUSINESS
future needs. In terms of Promotion, through advanced visualization capabilities, the platform presents
planning outcomes in an immersive digital environment, effectively bridging the gap between concept
and reality for stakeholders. In terms of Project, the platform’s green building and construction
capabilities enable real-time monitoring of construction progress while simulating environmental
impact, energy consumption, and resource utilization, helping achieve sustainable development goals.
Additionally, in terms of Program, its safe operation and management features provide comprehensive
monitoring of urban infrastructure operations, integrating real-time data from multiple sources to
enable predictive maintenance and risk management. These capabilities, built upon our unified urban
database, form a comprehensive solution that advances urban development efficiency while promoting
sustainability.
The city digital infrastructure is not a traditional CIM platform. Rather, it is based on the
current state of the city and the overall planning, and can interact with multi-dimensional indicators
such as demographics, economy, architecture, industry, transportation, supporting facilities, finance,
and more. We will also be implementing simulation to transform the planning process from static to
dynamic.Bydoingso,wewillbecreatingnewdigitaltwinsanddataelements,whichwillserveasthe
foundation for a new quality productivity standard. We believe this will empower people to live better
livesanddrivethenextphaseofurbanrenewalandconstruction.
Leveraging 51Earth’s real-time generation and update technology, we aim to launch a new
generation of AES6 city baseboard products, with WDP providing fully localized hardware and
operatingsystemsupport.Furthermore,weintendtoexpandthenumberofWDPdevelopers,introduce
three new digital infrastructure layouts for large and medium-sized cities on an annual basis via the
51CIM platform, sustain customer growth through the 51CIM platform, and concentrate the 51WIM
platformonservicingmajorwaterinstitutionsinChina.
Our51XIMplatformisalsodesignedtotargetenterprisesalignedwiththeMadeinChina2025
initiative and the digital upgrade needs of China’s major power grids. Made in China 2025 serves as
the first ten-year action plan in China’s strategy to become a global manufacturing powerhouse. The
primary objective of current phase is to enhance the manufacturing capability through specific
measures, including manufacturing process simulation, digital control and real-time monitoring. The
51XIM platform leverages digital twin technology to construct real-time and comprehensive 3D
models, enabling the manufacturing companies to simulate the manufacturing process and conduct
digital control and real-time monitoring on the platform. For example, as demonstrated in our
collaboration with China Railway Engineering Equipment Group detailed in “Business — Our
ProductsandSolutions—AES—51XIM:IndustrialandEnergyInformationModeling”,ourplatform
enables comprehensive digital twin modeling of shield machine production, integrating data from
personnel, vehicles, equipment, and the environment to optimize manufacturing processes and ensure
production safety. Additionally, the 51XIM platform also facilitates the construction of electric grids
by simulating the power grid construction process and conducting real-time monitoring, enabling
intelligent decision-making and preventing potential risks that could occur during construction. As of
the Latest Practicable Date, we are engaged in over 30 projects with key stakeholders in the power
sectorfortheconstructionofpowergrids,powerstations,andelectricalsubstations.
Additionally, the 51Aes platform integrates digital twin geological baseboards with geological
disaster early warning models to enable the visualization of underground resources, which can
significantly enhance the understanding, management, and disaster early warning capabilities of
undergroundspaces.Bydoingso,wecanprovideefficientdecision-makingsupportformultiplefields,

Expandglobalmarketreachwithdigitaltwinsolutions
We anticipate substantial market opportunities for digital twin solutions in global market.

management applications such as real-time traffic status monitoring, elevator operation monitoring,
bridgehealthmanagement,floodsimulation,andweathersimulation.

city development. Our solutions integrates IoT-enabled sensing and control systems, visualization
capabilities,spatialanalysistools,simulationandvirtual-physicalinteractionfeatures.Bytargetingkey
urban areas such as public services, public safety, and precision governance, we will continue to make
contributions to Turkey’s smart city initiatives while providing a replicable model for global urban
innovation.
In Australia, we have partnered with the University of Melbourne to develop a smart campus
project. This project involves creating a virtual version of the university’s new campus using real
geographic information, integrating elements such as environmental data, road networks, campus
layouts,andbuildingtypes.Byintroducingavirtualmulti-dimensionalmanagementsystem,weaimto
establish new standards for intelligent campus operations that can be replicated at educational
institutionsworldwide.

51AES
51Aes aims to help customers quickly build digital twin scenes through digital twin platform,
facilitatingdigitaltransformationacrossallindustries.

UnderlyingComponents
(cid:129) AllElementsScene(AES)
On the basis of real physical elements, AES is able to faithfully simulate 3D scenes with
computer graphics and AI, to realize real-time rendering of ultra-large-scale scenes and individualized
managementofallelements.
Relying on computer graphics, big data, cloud computing and other technologies, AES can
automatically or semi-automatically construct a digital twin world. AES can quickly convert various
modelfilesdescribingtherealphysicalworldintovirtualscenesofthedigitaltwinscene,suchas:
(cid:129) Automatedgenerationbased onsatelliteorthophotosandGISdata:AIalgorithmscan
automaticallygenerateurbanscenesfromorthographicimagesandGISdata.
(cid:129) Reconstruction and generation based on OSGB data: Computer semantic recognition
algorithm can automatically lightweight reconstruct based on oblique photography / lidar
scanning.
(cid:129) Automated generation based on BIM data: Automated transformation and generation
based on BIM models, while retaining the catalogs and attributes of all components and
parts.
(cid:129) Procedural generation of specific scenes: Rapid generation of specific scenes based on
proceduralalgorithms,suchastransmissionstationsandpowergrids.
(cid:129) Constructing based on massive digital asset library: Rapidly build scenes based on
matchingthefeaturesfrommassivedigitalassetlibrary.
(cid:129) Reconstruction and generation based on photo topology: 3D topology reconstruction
andgenerationmodelbasedonrealphotos.
(cid:129) RapidconstructionbasedonSaaSplatform:SecondaryeditingofscenesbasedonSaaS
platform.

We divide the applications of AES into five stages: V1 visualizing, V2 data fusing, V3 data
driving,V4simulating,andV5intelligentdecision-making.Afteryearsoftechnicaltrialsandpractical
applications, we have successfully implemented cases in each stage according to different
requirements. V1 visualizing refers to reconstructing real-world scenarios into three-dimensional
visualizations from vector data. V2 data fusing refers to integrating business data directly into scenes
or business panels to improve understanding and application efficiency. V3 data driving refers to
connectingIoTandotherdynamicallycollecteddatatodrivemodelsinreal-time,synchronizingdigital
twin behaviors with reality (such as production line data animating mechanical arms). V4 simulating
refers to generating autonomous decision-making mechanisms for intelligent agents to model their
behaviors and movements (like simulating crowd evacuation). V5 intelligentdecision-making refers to
combining digital twin and simulation technologies to model different outcomes based on varying
parameters and autonomously determine optimal solutions, though this stage remains in exploration
andhasnotyetbeenformallyimplemented.
DigitalTwinSaaSPlatform(WDP)
WDP is a user-friendly, digital twin application and development platform that provides
developers with features such as multi-source data import, intuitive scene creation, low-code
development,openAPIs,andotherdigitaltwindevelopmentservices.
OurWDP platformhas undergone multipleiterations,evolvingfromversion1.0toversion5.0,
with each upgrade introducing enhancements in functionality and application scope. Starting with
WDP1.0, which delivered cloud rendering and multi-device simultaneous display, WDP2.0 introduced
191

=== PAGE 201 ===
BUSINESS
a user and data management system along with support for virtualized deployment. WDP3.0 further
advancedtheplatformbyintegratingdigitaltwindevelopmentinterfaces(basedonJavaScriptscripting
language) and digital twin low-code development tools (designed for users without coding skills,
allowing program logic implementation through drag-and-drop node connections), offering a
comprehensive one-stop development toolkit for third-party digital twin application developers. With
WDP4.0, a digital twin asset library and basic scene editor were added, while WDP5.0 integrated
AES6 dynamic baseboard, real-time editing capabilities, and enabled industry-specific functionalities
such as CIM, WIM, and XIM. Additionally, WDP5.0 achieved over a 50% performance improvement
in its development interface compared to the previous version and fully supports localized trusted
computing environments. Each iteration of the WDP platform is designed to deliver improved features
andbroaderapplicationscenarios,drivinginnovationandtheadoptionofdigitaltwintechnologies.
Leveraging our extensive experience and technology in digital twin services across various
fields, we introduced WDP to offer a flexible, efficient, and versatile tool platform. It can be used by
industry end-users or secondary development customers to develop digital twin scenarios with
relatively low complexity, thereby reducing development costs. This not only lowers the cost for
customers but also boosts market demand for digital twin solutions, expands market scale, promotes
businessinnovation,andenhancesthecompetitivenessofourproducts.
WDPcanindependentlygenerate3Dbaseboardsbasedonspatialandtemporaldata,supporting
in-depth applications such as continuous scene updates, mass rendering, and secondary development.
The platform is user-friendly, easy to build with, flexible to expand, and compatible with multi-end
technology. It can be applied in various fields such as urban planning, parks and buildings, industry
and energy, water and environment, meeting diverse business needs like macro-planning, fine
management,andsimulation.
KeycompetitiveadvantagesofWDPinclude:
(cid:129) Digital assets generated on-demand: WDP generates tailored 3D digital platforms with
L2 regional-level and L3 scene-level accuracy based on spatiotemporal data, supporting
the rapid conversion and high-fidelity restoration of industry-specific 3D models in 15
different formats. It also enables users to autonomously create city base stations with L2
regional-level and L3 scene-level accuracy, complemented by AI intelligent completion
thatprovidesmorecomprehensivedataelementsandcompletespatialrepresentation.
(cid:129) Freestyle twin scenes construction: Users can rapidly create twin scenes using a vast
library of digital assets and user models. The platform supports the autonomous import
and free placement of high-precision 3D models, and non-linear editing allows for
efficient,unconstrained,andflexiblecreationofthesescenes.

(cid:129) XIL Solution: The XIL solution is a bunch of testing solutions used for testing
autonomous driving technology, helping to evaluate the performance of autonomous
driving systems in different environments. It consists of four main types: Software-in-
the-Loop (SIL), which tests the performance of the autonomous driving software in a
simulation environment; Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL), which connects the actual
hardware with the simulation environment to check the collaboration between hardware
and software; Driver-in-the-Loop (DIL), where a real driver interacts with the
autonomous driving system to assess its usability and adaptability; and Vehicle-in-the-
Loop (VIL), which brings a real vehicle into the test environment to examine the
performance of the autonomous driving system on an actual vehicle. These solutions
ensures the reliability and safety of autonomous driving technology at different
developmentstages.
SimOne significantly reduces testing costs, improves efficiency, and accelerates the production
of autonomous vehicles and robots. It enables extensive testing and validation in various scenarios,
such as weather conditions, road situations and traffic dynamics, without the risks and costs of real-
world testing. It facilitates rapid optimization and continuous enhancement of intelligent driving
systems, ensuring better performance and safety. SimOne is committed to providing robust software
solutions,empoweringdeveloperstorefinealgorithmsandcomprehensivelytestsystems.

TIM

requires extensive customization to deliver tailored implementations that address each customer’s
unique requirements, challenges and infrastructure. TIM comprises three major subsystems: the
construction of spatial and temporal elements of transportation (TIM Datalink), multi-level integrated
transportation simulation platform (TIM), and training and application services for large-scale
transportationmodels(TIMTransAI).

dataneededforvarioustypesofcalculations.

simulation, while TIM OS is tailored towards traffic operational management, primarily
drivenbyreal-timetrafficdata.

(cid:129) TIM TransAI: is an exploratoryapplication ofa general large modelinthe transportation
industry. It has formed a product architecture consisting of traffic perception, traffic
cognition, traffic prediction, and traffic knowledge graph. Traffic Perception refers to
providing synthetic data for training computer vision-related algorithms, applicable to the
training and iteration of traffic perception algorithms. Traffic Cognition involves using
large amounts of collected real traffic trajectory data to train and build AI traffic agents
through deep reinforcement learning, applicable to real traffic reconstruction and tracing.
Traffic Prediction uses historical traffic statistical data to forecast and simulate future
traffic flow, speed, demand, and accidents over a certain period, applicable to traffic
management, logistics management, and other fields. Traffic Knowledge Graph utilizes
LLM technology to build a traffic language assistant, assisting traffic simulation software
in quickly responding to user needs, summarizing documents, and other auxiliary
functions.

underlying issues and root causes. The objective is to facilitate decision-making in planning,

BUSINESS
Supported by a wealth of digital assets, 51Earth aims to revolutionize the creation of 3D
content by eliminating barriers, sparking creativity, and fostering innovation within a vibrant
community. It will bridge builders, developers, and consumers, offering unparalleled 3D and video
contentcraftedbyanewgenerationofcreators.
The primary users of 51Earth are intended to be game techies who are passionate about
building, developing, and exploring the digital Earth. 51Earth.com provides them with the tools and
community they need to bring their innovative visions to life. This dynamic ecosystem will ensure a
constant flow of fresh, quality 3D experiences, which will in turn attract a vibrant consumer audience
forthesedigitalexperiences.
As users immerse themselves in the captivating world of 51Earth, the platform will benefit
from revenues from subscription and value-added services. The more time consumers spend on
51Earth,thegreatertheopportunitiesforgrowthandprofit.
First launched in 2022, 51Earth first focused on providing a VR or metaverse platform for
enterprises, bringing new experiences to corporate marketing activities. Through high-precision scene
rendering and real-time cloud rendering technology, it helps clients create immersive presentation and
interaction spaces that blend virtual and real elements. With content creation and visual experiences, it
creates a 3D virtual world for users that combines entertainment, knowledge, and interactivity. During
the Track Record Period, substantially all revenue from 51Earth was generated from such VR and
metaverse offerings. Specific applications include online meeting and digital exhibition halls. 51Earth
has since then evolved into an enhanced platform in 2024, marked by the launch of 51Earth.com on
March1,2024,offeringfreeaccessto51EarthBuilderand51EarthDevKitonJuly1,2024.
We provide the following digital assets and tools for builders and developers to facilitate the
developmentoftheecosystem:
DigitalAssets
UrbanGeneralAsset(UGA)
UGA provides a comprehensive library of large-scale, highlyscalable and interactive 3D urban
environmentmodelssuchasbuildings,skyscrapers,roads,urbangreenspaces,suburbanenvironments,
forests and lakes etc., allowing developers to rapidly create video and 3D applications based on large-
scale urban scenes by secondary development on mainstream engines such as Unreal and WDP. UGA
supportsmodularizeddesign,enablingdeveloperstofreelyselect,add,removeormodifyeachelement
atruntime,ensuringsmoothsupportforover1millionelementsandover100,000squarekilometersof
scenes. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we have released UGA assets for Dubai, Singapore, Riyadh
andJeddah,readytouseandenrichingdevelopers’creativeresources.
DigitalTwinAssets(DTA)
DTA provides users with a useful and flexible library of 3D virtual representations that model
physical objects and systems. These digital twins meet a variety of 3D content development needs.
DTA adopts the GLTF format as its foundation, ensuring the integrity and high compatibility of 3D
information,andsupportingseamlessmigrationfrommodelingsoftwaretogameengines,significantly
improving work efficiency. Through unified cloud management, DTA assets can be viewed and
referenced by developers anytime, anywhere, enhancing resource utilization and development
convenience.

OurR&DProcess
We independently conduct product research and development based on technology and market
trends. The R&D projects follow a standardized software development process and produce core
results through internal testing and release. This process includes four main stages: research, project
initiation,development,andprojectcompletion.
FeasibilityStudyPhase
Requirements Collection: Product managers analyze and summarize user requirements,
conductmarketresearch,andcompetitiveanalysis.

BUSINESS
Feasibility Studies: R&D personnel perform technical research on relevant general and
specializedtechnologiestoprepareforatechnicalfeasibilitystudy.
ProjectPhase
Project Preparation: Based on the Feasibility Study Report, the productmanager analyzes the
background, investment reasonableness, feasibility, and advancement of the R&D project. The R&D
leader summarizes the main R&D content, implementation plan, overall budget, and staffing plan,
formingtheR&DProjectReport.
Project Approval Meeting: Attended by heads of product, R&D, finance, legal, and HR. The
product manager presents the project’s rationale and feasibility, while the R&D leader presents the
implementationplanandbudget.Onceapprovedbyalldepartments,thereportissubmittedtotheCEO
forfinalapproval.

R&DIteration:
Follows an agile development process with multiple iterations. Product managers design and

(functional,performance,interface,security)toensurequality.
Product managers prepare project overviews, completion reports, and collaborate on product

ProjectCompletionPhase

standardization.

INTELLECTUALPROPERTY
We rely on unpatented trade secrets, confidential know-how, and continuous technological
innovation, to develop, strengthen, and maintain our competitive position. We seek to protect and
enhance our proprietary technologies, inventions, and improvements that are commercially important
to the growth of our business, including by seeking, maintaining, and defending patent rights. We also
strive to operate without infringing, misappropriating or otherwise violating the intellectual property
rightsofthirdparties.Inthedevelopmentofproductsandsolutions,weleverageself-createddata,data
purchased from suppliers and data provided by customers. The intellectual property rights to 3D
models created from supplier-provided data belong to us. For custom 3D models we create for
customers, the intellectual property rights default to us, unless the customer expressly requests
ownership or co-ownership and we confirm that we have no model reuse requirements, in which case
thecustomermayholdtheownershiprightsorco-ownwithus.Anillustrativeexampleofthissituation
iswhereacustomerrequiresustocreatea3Dmodelorsimulationofaspecificroadwithinoradjacent
to their facility. In such cases, we typically have no model reuse requirements for this specific
customized asset and can therefore agree to the customer’s request for ownership rights. This
ownership arrangement generally does not result in material pricing differences compared to scenarios
whereweretaintheintellectualpropertyrights.
It is important to our future commercial success that we obtain and maintain patent and other
proprietary protection for commercially important technology, inventions, and know-how related to
our business; defend and enforce our IP rights, in particular our patents, trademarks, and copyrights;
maintain the confidentiality of our trade secrets; and operate without infringing, misappropriating, or
violatingthe validand enforceablepatentsandproprietaryrightsofthirdparties.Ourabilitytoprevent
third parties from making, using, selling, offering to sell, or importing any technology products we
developmaydependontheextenttowhichwehaverightsundervalidandenforceablepatentsortrade
secretscoveringtheseactivities.
The patent landscape for companies such as ours is generally uncertain and can involve
complex legal, scientific, and factual issues. We cannot predict whether the patent applications we
havefiledwillresultinissuedpatentsinanyparticularjurisdictionorwhethertheclaimsofanyissued
patents will provide sufficient proprietary protection from competitors. Furthermore, we cannot
guarantee the issuance of patents for any future patent applications, nor can we ensure that any of our
patents, present or future, will be effective in protecting our software, technology, computational
platform, and any product candidates we develop. In addition, the coverage claimed in a patent
application may be significantly reduced before a patent is issued, and its scope can be reinterpreted
and even challenged after issuance. As a result, we cannot guarantee that any technology products we
develop will be protected or remain protectable by enforceable patents. Moreover, any patents that we
hold or may hold may be challenged, circumvented or invalidated by third parties. See “Risk
Factors—Risks Relating to Our Intellectual Property Rights” for a more comprehensive description of
risksrelatedtoourIP.

COMPETITION
China’s digital twin solution market is experiencing rapid growth, and the current competitive
landscapeisfragmented,withnumeroustypesofplayersofferingadiverserangeofsolutions.
Players in the China digital twin solution market can be categorized into two types: one-stop
solution providers and point solution providers. One-stop solution providers are equipped to offer a
comprehensive range of products and services, spanning model asset development tools to
applications, and digital twin applications across multiple domains. In contrast, point solution
providers specialize in a specific type of product or service and offer digital twin applications within a
single domain. One-stop solution providers have a number of significant advantages over point
solution providers, including greater technical capabilities, technical comprehensiveness, industry
knowledge,businessmodeldiversity,andgrowthpotential.
For more information about our competitive strengths, our industry and the risks we face,
please refer to the sections headed “Industry Overview” and “Risk factors—Risks Related to Our
Business and Industry—We operate inhighlycompetitive markets and some market participants may
have substantially greater resources. We compete against a large number of both established
competitorsandnewmarketentrants.”includedelsewhereinthisprospectus.

Sales to system integrators typically occur when end users decide to use system integrators to
save them from the trouble of directly negotiating with a large number of different suppliers or service
providers. Such end users typically lay out the goals they plan to achieve and the budget for their
projects and engage third-party system integrators, instead of engaging us directly. When competing
for projects from end users, system integrators sometimes invite us and other suppliers to join the
tender process. We may be required to work closely with system integrators and other suppliers to
ensure compatibility of our products and solutions with the overall project. During the Track Record
Period, we did not enter into any exclusivity agreements with system integrators. To the best of our
knowledge, it is also not common practice in our industry to enter into such agreements with system
integrators.
While many system integrators offer diverse product lines, they often partner with specialized
companies like ours in specific domains such as digital twin technology, where our specialized
expertise and diverse solutions give us a competitive advantage. System integrators value our
company’s specialized digital twin expertise while we benefit from their established relationships with
end-users and ability to deliver complete solutions, creating a mutually beneficial partnership that
drives our growing system integrator revenue stream. System integrators frequently choose to
outsource digital twin components to third-party suppliers with deeper domain expertise rather than
developing these specialized capabilities in-house. For example, in a national museum’s digital
operations intelligent control platform project, we provided digital twin business support for the smart
park operations management platform. Similarly, for a reservoir project in Sichuan, we delivered
knowledge bases, hydraulic professional modellibraries, and floodprevention forecasting systems that
formed a comprehensive visualization dashboard digital twin system covering the reservoir. In the
typical workflowwithsystemintegrators,end-usersfirstengagetheintegrator,whothenevaluates and
selects appropriate technology providers (includingourCompany)based onprojectspecifications. The
integrator manages the entire implementation process, including integration of our digital twin
platform with other systems. According to Frost & Sullivan, cooperation with system integrators is
commonpracticeintheenterprisesolutionsector,particularlyforcomplexsolutionsrequiringmultiple
specializedcomponentsfromdifferentvendors.
In addition, in certain instances, we also act as the system integrator or coordinator (or sub-
integrator),wherebeyondprovidingourowndigitaltwinproductsandsolutions,weneedtocoordinate
complementary services or systems of other suppliers that are essential to delivering a complete and
functional project. During the Track Record Period, we were only involved in the role of system
integratorinone smart village project and served as sub-integratorinseveral otherprojects.Inthe said
smart village project where we served as the system integrator, our professional and diverse internal
teams conduct on-site fieldwork where, through systematic surveys, questionnaires, and structured
group interviews, they comprehensively assess the current state of village infrastructure (roads, water,
electricity,internet),agriculturalproduction(cropandlivestockvarieties,scale,productionefficiency),
villagegovernance, andculturalheritage(folkactivities,historicalsites).Based onthisassessment, we
develop strategic project plans that not only align with the village’s practical realities but also
incorporate long-term forward-thinking perspectives, clearly defining the project’s phased objectives,
technical roadmap, and implementation steps. We then coordinate selected partners, includingnetwork
222

=== PAGE 232 ===

communication providers, hardware suppliers, data platform providers, and rural business system
developers with various capabilities, to collaboratively establish a comprehensive and functional
digital twin foundation for the village. After we establish this comprehensive digital twin foundation,
thesolutionistypicallyfurtherintegratedintotheoverallprojectarchitecturebytheprimaryintegrator,
who ensures seamless compatibility with broader system components and aligns our specialized
contribution with the project’s overall objectives. Within this integrated approach, the overall project
architecture encompasses far more than just our digital twin foundation. It includes the complete
ecosystem of technologies and systems: physical infrastructure components (such as sensors,
networking hardware, and IoT devices - other than those involved in our digital twin solution),
application layers (including specialized management software for different village sectors such as
land resource management systems, agricultural production planning, environmental monitoring and
soil testing), data integration frameworks, security systems, user interfaces, and connected service
platforms from various providers. Our digital twin foundation functions as one specialized technical
layer that enables virtual modeling and simulation, while the primary integrator coordinates how this
foundation interacts with these broader architectural elements to create a cohesive, functioning smart
villagesystem.

software update. As a matter of policy, only hardware components with defects may be returned.

defects and typically offer us warranty which corresponds to the warranty period we provide to our
customers. Some of our customers may require a retention amount (typically 3% to 10% of the total
contract value) as security against product quality during the warranty period. This retained portion is
released and payable by the customer after we have successfully fulfilled our warranty obligations
uponexpirationofthewarrantyperiod.
Pricing
We price our solutions and services considering a variety of factors, such as our contract
fulfillment costs, the value of our solutions or services to the customer, the scarcity of our solutions or
services in the market, the urgency of the delivery of our solutions or services, our delivery capacity,
competition in the market, market’s willingness to pay, the overall market condition, and competitors’
pricing strategies. In some cases, particularly for innovative or forward-looking projects, both us and
our customers acknowledge inherent feasibility and implementation risks. For these projects with less
established implementation pathways, pricing may reflect our shared understanding of the innovative
natureandassociateduncertainties.Takingthesefactorsintoaccount,wemayadopteithercost-driving
pricing or target-return pricing for different solutions or services. During the Track Record Period, the
price ranges of our major products varied significantly primarily depending on the scale of
deployment, customization requirements, implementation complexity, computational requirements,
geographic coverage, and level of technical support needed. In terms of average contract size, for
51Aes, average contract size was approximately RMB0.9 million, RMB1.1 million, RMB1.8 million
and RMB1.0 million in 2022, 2023, and 2024, and for the six months ended June 30, 2025,
respectively. For 51Sim, average contract size was approximately RMB0.8 million, RMB1.0 million,
RMB1.0 million and RMB0.5 million in the same periods, respectively. For 51Earth, average contract
size was approximately RMB0.3 million, RMB0.6 million, RMB1.1 million and RMB0.4 million in
the same periods, respectively. The lower average contract size in the first half of 2025 compared to

SEASONALITY
We experience seasonality in our business, primarily because of seasonal fluctuations in
customer procurement demands. During the Track Record Period, we generally recorded higher
revenues for our products and solutions in the fourth quarter of the year, primarily because certain of
our customers tend to finalize their annual procurement schedules and budgets during the first quarter
of the year and complete their inspection and accept our products and solutions in the fourth quarter,
which cause us to recognize revenue in the fourth quarter according to relevant revenue recognition
policy. Throughout the year, we typically engage with customers to understand their requirements and
participate in project planning and design phases during earlier quarters, followed by solution delivery
in subsequent periods. According to Frost & Sullivan, this seasonal pattern is consistent with industry
norms and reflects the procurement and budgeting cycles typical of medium to large enterprises and
government entities in China. As such, we believe this pattern is likely to continue in the foreseeable
future. See “Risk Factors–Our business and results of operations are subject to seasonal fluctuations”
formoredetails.

OURSUPPLIERS
During the Track Record Period, our suppliers mainly consisted of hardware vendors, such as
all-in-one PCs and specialized equipment, and software vendors, such as scene design, art rendering,
system development and digital model modeling. We provide products and solutions on a project-by-
projectbasis,andthereforesoftwareorsoftwareserviceprocurementcouldbeaffectedbythedifferent
requirements of projects we work on from time to time. During the Track Record Period, software
suppliers provided various software or software services such as 3D model editing, interactive
interface, cloud resources, mid-end and back-end system development etc. While we purchase certain
softwarefromsuchsoftwarevendors,suchsoftwarearemainlyusedforthedevelopmentorintegration
with our products and solutions and not for reselling purposes. Purchases from our five largest
suppliersofrespective year/periodin2022,2023and2024andforthesixmonthsendedJune30,2025
amounted to RMB46.5 million, RMB10.7 million, RMB34.4 million and RMB17.2 million,
respectively, representing 63.9%, 41.9%, 32.7% and 71.5% of our total purchases in the same year/
period, respectively. All of our five largest suppliers in each year/period during the Track Record
Period were located in the PRC. Our products and solutions are mainly offered on a project-by-project
basis and therefore our procurement from our five largest suppliers for each year/period during the
Track Record Period may fluctuate based on specific conditions and requirements of projects ongoing
at the time. Our purchases from our five largest suppliers of respective year/period in 2022 was
relatively higher than in 2023 and 2024 primarily due to the significant procurement amount from
Supplier A which accounted for approximately 43.4% of our total purchases in 2022. In connection
with our project with Customer F (our largest customer in 2023), we procured over 600 servers from
Supplier A to integrate our digital twin solutions with Customer F’s GPUs. In connection with our
project with Customer J, for the six months ended June 30, 2025, Supplier N contributed to
approximately 39.8% of our total procurement during the period. For details of our project with
CustomerFandCustomerJ,see“—Ourcustomers”above.

CUSTOMERSLISTEDONTHEENTITYLIST
In recent years, the United States has increased export controls restrictions on China through
the Export Administration Regulations (the “EAR”), administered by the Bureau of Industry and
Security (the “BIS”) of the U.S. Department of Commerce, which includes a list of foreign persons on
which certain trade restrictions are imposed, including businesses, research institutions, government
and private organizations, individuals and other types of legal persons (the “Entity List”). When a
foreign person is included on the Entity List, the export, re-export and/or transfer (in-country)of items
which are subject to the EAR generally is prohibited unless the specified license requirements are met.
CertainofourcustomersandshareholdersarelistedontheEntityList:(i)Entity1asourcustomer,(ii)
Entity 2 as a shareholder of our Company and (iii) Entity 3 as a shareholder of our Company and a
customer (collectively referred to as the “Relevant Entities”). These restrictions can limit their
operationalcapabilitiesandaffectthesecustomers’demandsforourproductsandsolutions.

TRANSFERPRICINGARRANGEMENTS
During the tracking period, we primarily conducted our business through subsidiaries in China
and established subsidiaries in overseas jurisdictions to expand our international market operations.
During the same period, our international intra-group transactions mainly included: (i) software
customization development services provided by Wanjing Xiangjing Technology (Chengdu) Co., Ltd.
under the entrustment of Beijing 51world Digital Twin Technology Co., Ltd., ultimately completing
service delivery to customers; and (ii) overseas orders undertaken by 51VR PTY Ltd., which entrusted
Beijing 51world Digital Twin Technology Co., Ltd. to provide software development and technical
supportservices(collectivelyreferredtoasthe“CoveredTransactions”).
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (“OECD”), as an international
organization for international cooperation, has promulgated the “OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines
for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations” (the “OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines”),
which are generally followed by relevant tax jurisdictions involved in international intra-group
transactions. According to the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, intra-group transactions should
adhere to the arm’s length principle to prevent the distortion of taxable income in different tax
jurisdictions.
We have engaged Transfer Pricing Advisor to conduct a transfer pricing review and
benchmarking study for the Covered Transactions during the tracking period to assess whether our
transfer pricing arrangements comply with the arm’s length principle of the OECD Transfer Pricing
Guidelines. The Transfer Pricing Advisor performed an independent analysis and concluded that,
during the Track Record Period, the transfer pricing arrangements for the Covered Transactions were
incompliancewiththearm’slengthprincipleoftheOECDTransferPricingGuidelinesonthebasisof,
(i) the selection of appropriate transfer pricing methods (cost-plus method and profit split method)
based on the functional and risk profiles of each party; (ii) comparability analyses demonstrating that
the profit margins fall within the arm’s length range; and (iii) value contribution analyses confirming
thatprofitallocationsreflectthefunctionsperformedandrisksassumedbyeachparty.

StrategicOutsourcingofNon-coreActivities:
(cid:129) High-precision 3D Modeling: We strategically outsource 3D modeling services for

component-level models) to specialized vendors. These precision levels require

highly labor-intensive with relatively low profit margins. This allows our core team
to focus on developing the digital twin engine and platform products. According to

thedigitaltwinanddigitalizationindustries.

DATAPRIVACYANDSECURITY
We are committed to complyingwithdata privacy laws and protectingthe security ofcustomer
data. We have appointed a Head of Cyber Security, a Head of Data Security and a Head of Personal
Information Protection, who are responsible for the company’s cyber security and data protection. The
types of data handled by our Group mainly include the self-created data, the data purchased from
suppliers, and the data generated by customers using our products. Self-created data primarily include
3D models generated and accumulated by us through the years of our operations such as general 3D
models of trees, buildings and other daily objects. Data from suppliers and customers include physical
data,energydata,environmentaldata(water/air/noise),andtrafficdataandtrafficflow,etc.Fordetails
ofallocation ofintellectual propertyrightsderivedfromthird-partydata,see “—IntellectualProperty.”
Suppliers of data primarily include companies providing aerial photography services, surveying and
mapping data and similar services or products. During the course of our business during the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we do not engage in surveying or mapping
activities and are not involved in the processing of surveying and mapping data in the context of the
Surveying and Mapping Law of the PRC. We acquire and apply in the development of our solutions
such data from suppliers with surveying and mapping qualifications and these suppliers only provide
data to us after it has been shifted or de-identified and is no longer considered surveying and mapping
data. With respect to customer data, all access to geographic information such as high-precision maps
and satellite imagery occurs exclusively within client environments and we neither download, export
nor store such data. Regarding the data visualization functionalities of our products and solutions, we
onlyread real-timedata onlinethroughcustomer data center interfaces and donotdownload,exportor
store such data. According to our PRC Legal Advisor, none of the type of data handled by the Group
areclassifiedasimportantdataandthepersonalinformationthatwecollectandhandlemainlyconsists
of personal information related to users’ registration and use of our products, including name, mobile
phone number, etc. The personal information collected and processed by the Group includes user’s
registration and login information through providing services. Such personal information is necessary
for the realization of products or services. Before collecting users’ personal information, we provide a

LegalProceedings
From time to time, we may become involved in legal proceedings and claims that arise in the

On June 21, 2024, one of our service providers filed an arbitration against our Company,
alleging breach of contract. During the Track Record Period, the service provider provided us with
cloud hosting services. The claimant is seeking approximately RMB23 million in monetary damages
from our Company. Additionally, the claimant submitted an application for property preservation
corresponding to the claimed amount in our bank accounts, which has been approved. We intend to
defend ourselves vigorously on the basis that we believe the claimant’s allegations are without merit.
Thefundamentaldisputearosefromtheclaimant’sfailuretomeetservicequalitystandardsdespitethat
wehavepaidpartialservicefeesinaccordancewiththerelevantagreementwiththeclaimant.
On October 23, 2024, we filed counterclaims against the claimant for breach of contract,
seeking recovery of paid service fees and othermonetary damages. Despite having paid approximately
RMB4 million for services that consistently failed to meet contractual specifications, with recurring
equipment malfunctions and inadequate platform performance, the claimant has not only failed to
remedy these issues but has also taken aggressive legal measures including freezing ourbank accounts
through property preservation applications. As permitted under Article 577 of the Civil Code of the
PRC,wearepursuingappropriateremediesthrougharbitrationtocounterclaimasumofapproximately
RMB4.2 million, comprising the aforementioned paid service fees and monetary compensation for
damages resulting from the claimant’s material breaches. The first arbitration hearing was held on
December21,2024.

SocialInsuranceandHousingProvidentFunds

and housing provident fund contributions administered by competent government authorities. During
the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, (i) we were not in strict compliance
with the contribution requirements in relation to our employees because we did not make social
insurance and housing provident fund contributions in full amount based on the actual salary for some
ofouremployees,(ii)wedidnotcompletetherelevantemployeebenefitplanregistrationsforsomeof
our subsidiaries in China either because the relevant subsidiaries did not have any employee or made
the social insurance and housing fund contributions through third-party agencies, and (iii) we engaged
third-party agencies to make such contributions on our behalf for certain employees, which, although
not uncommon in China, was not in strict compliance with applicable PRC laws and regulations
according to our PRC Legal Advisor, primarily because these employees were located in cities where
we did not have any registered operating entities. Specifically, we engaged two human resource
agencies for such third-party arrangements for 13 employees as of June 30, 2025. We hired employees
in relevant location and adopted such arrangement for business development needs in these cities. The
aggregate shortfall of social insurance payments and housing provident fund contributions in 2022,
2023 and 2024 and for the six months ended June 30, 2025 amounted to approximately
RMB9.9million,RMB14.7million,RMB16.8millionandRMB8.2million,respectively.Theincrease
during the Track Record Period was primarily due to the increase in the number of incumbent
employeeswithsocialinsuranceandhousingprovidentfundshortfalls.Wehavemadefullprovisionin
connection with social insurance shortfalls. The accumulated provisions we made on our financial

forthesixmonthsendedJune30,2025.

Accoding to the Social Insurance Law of the PRC, if an employer fails to register for social
insurance, the social insurance administrative department shall order it to make corrections within a
specified period. If the employer fails to make corrections within the specified period, it shall be fined
between one and three times the amount of the social insurance premium payable. Additionally, the
directlyresponsiblemanagersandotherdirectlyresponsiblepersonnelshallbefinedbetweenRMB500
and RMB3,000. If an employer fails to pay social insurance premiums in full and on time, the social
insurance collection agency shall order it to pay or make up the amount within a specified period and
impose a late fee of 0.05% of the overdue amount per day starting from the date of default. If the
payment is still not made within the specified period, the relevant administrative department shall
impose a fine of one to three times the overdue amount. According to the Regulations on the
Administration of Housing Provident Funds (2019 Revision), if an employer fails to register for
housing provident fund contributions or fails to establish housing provident fund accounts for its
employees, the housing provident fund management center shall order it to complete the procedures
within a specified period. If the employer fails to comply within the specified period, it shall be fined
between RMB10,000 and RMB50,000. If an employer delays or underpays housing provident fund
contributions,thehousingprovidentfundmanagementcentershallorderittomakethepaymentwithin
a specified period. If the payment is still not made within the specified period, the management center
may apply to the People’s Court for compulsory enforcement. Furthermore, as advised by our PRC
Legal Advisor, if the validity of our arrangement with third-party agencies is challenged by competent
PRC authorities, we might be subject to additional contributions, late payment fees and/or penalties
required by relevant PRC laws and regulations for failing to discharge our obligations in relation to
payment of social insurance and housing provident funds as an employer or be ordered to rectify such
practice.
As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had not received any notice for payment of penalties of
social insurance premium and housing provident funds from the competent authorities. Administrative
enforcement authorities are prohibited from organizing and conducting centralized collection of
enterprises’ historical social insurance arrears. In addition, Mr. Li has agreed to indemnify the
Company for any losses the Company may suffer as a result of the shortfall in the contribution. As
advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, the likelihood of us receiving any notice of penalties from the
competent authorities is relatively low, provided that we pay the outstanding contribution, and late fee
(if any), for social insurance and house provident funds in full amount within the prescribed period
after receiving notices to rectify such non-compliance from the competent authorities. Pursuant to the
Urgent Notice on Enforcing the Requirement of the General Meeting of the State Council and
Stabilizing the Levy of Social Insurance Payment (《關於貫徹落實國務院常務會議精神切實做好穩定社
保費徵收工作的緊急通知》) promulgated on September 21, 2018 by the Ministry of Human Resources
and Social Security, administrative enforcement authorities are prohibited from organizing and
conducting aggregated collection of enterprises’ historical social insurance arrears. As advised by our
PRC Legal Advisor, if we receive notices from the competent authorities requiring us to rectify such
non-compliance, and we pay such outstanding amounts and late fees (if any) within the required
period,thelikelihoodofusbeingrequiredtopaypenaltiesisremote.

OVERVIEW
We are a digital twin technology company in China. We have invested heavily in and
developedcorecompetenciesintechnologyaroundthreemajorareas:3Dgraphics,simulation,andAI.
We aim to provide eco-partners including enterprises, consumers and developers with solutions to
access andbuilddigitaltwinsandworktogetherwiththemtocreatea“DigitalTwinEarth”whichwill
in the end enhance the efficiency, safety, and quality of the real world as well as provide people with
newperspectivesandtechnologiestounderstandandimproveourworld.
During the Track Record Period, our revenue grew significantly. Our revenue increased by
50.8% fromRMB170.0 millionin2022toRMB256.3 millionin2023,and furtherincreased by12.1%
to RMB287.4 million in 2024. Our revenue increased by 62.0% from RMB33.2 million for the six
monthsendedJune30,2024toRMB53.8millionforthesameperiodin2025.

CRITICALACCOUNTINGPOLICIES,JUDGMENTSANDESTIMATES
Some of our accounting policies require us to apply estimates and assumptions as well as
complex judgments relating to accounting items. The estimates and assumptions that we use and the
judgments that we make in applying our accounting policies have a significant impact on our financial
condition and results of operations. Our management continually evaluates such estimates,
assumptions,andjudgmentsbasedonpastexperienceandotherfactors,includingexpectationoffuture
events that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. There has not been any material
deviation between our management’s estimates or assumptions and actual results, and we have not
made any material changes to these estimates or assumptions during the Track Record Period. We do
notexpectanymaterialchangesintheseestimatesandassumptionsintheforeseeablefuture.
Set forth below are discussions of the accounting policies that we believe are of critical
importance to us or involve the most significant estimates, assumptions, and judgments used in the
preparationofourfinancialstatements.Othermaterialaccountingpolicies,estimates,assumptions,and
judgments, which are importantforunderstandingourfinancialconditionandresultsofoperations,are
setforthindetailinNotes2and3totheAccountants’ReportinAppendixItothisprospectus.
Revenueandotherincome
Income is classified as revenue when it arises from the sale of goods or the provision of
servicesintheordinarycourseofourbusiness.
Furtherdetailsofourrevenueandotherincomerecognitionpoliciesareasfollows:
Revenuefromcontractswithcustomers
Revenue arising from the sale of software platform and also from the sale of software platform
together with software-embedded hardware as an integrated solution is accounted for as a single
performance obligation. Revenue is recognised at a point in time when the software and the hardware
(if applicable) are delivered to the customer’s designated place, inspected and accepted by the
customer. In other circumstance, the software platform is delivered to end users for usage with a
subscriptionperiod,therevenueisrecognizedoverthesubscriptionperiod.
The maintenance and upgrade services after sale are provided to maintain and improve the
effectiveness of the software and therefore are accounted for as a separate performance obligation and
arerecognisedovertheserviceperiod.
Revenuefromothersourcesandotherincome
(a) Dividends
Dividend income is recognised in profit or loss on the date on which our right to receive
paymentisestablished.
(b) Interestincome
Interestincomeisrecognisedusingtheeffectiveinterestmethod.The“effectiveinterestrate”is
the rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash receipts through the expected life of the financial
assettothegrosscarryingamountofthefinancialasset.

FINANCIALINFORMATION
(c) Governmentgrants
Government grants are recognized in the statement of financial position initially when there is
reasonable assurance that they will be received and that we will comply with the conditions attaching
to them. Grants that compensate us for expenses incurred are recognised as income in profit or loss on
a systematic basis in the same periods in which the expenses are incurred. Grants that compensate us
for the cost of an asset are recognised as deferred income in the statement of financial position and are
subsequentlyrecognisedinprofitorlossovertheusefullifeoftheasset.
Allowanceforcreditlosses
Management estimates credit loss allowance using a provision matrix based on our historical
credit loss experience, included customer credit-worthiness, and historical write-off experience, and
adjusted for factors that are specific to the debtors and an assessment of both the current and forecast
general economic conditions at the reporting date. If the financial conditions of the customers were to
deteriorate,additionalallowancemayberequired.
Inventoriesandothercontractcosts
Inventories
Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Cost is calculated using
the specific cost method and comprises all costs of purchase, costs of conversion and other costs
incurredinbringingtheinventoriestotheirpresentlocationandcondition.
Net realizable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less the
estimatedcostsofcompletionandtheestimatedcostsnecessarytomakethesale.
Othercontractcosts
Other contract costs are either the incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer or
the cost to fulfil a contract with a customer which are not capitalized as inventory, property and
equipmentorintangibleassets.
We take advantage of practical expedient in paragraph 94 of the IFRS 15 and recognizes the
incremental costs of obtaining a contract as an expense if the amortization of the asset that we
otherwisewouldhaverecognizedisoneyearorless.
Costs tofulfilla contract are capitalized ifthe costs related directlytoanexistingcontractorto
a specifically identifiable anticipated contract; generate or enhance resources that will be used to
provide goods or services in the future;and are expected tobe recovered. Otherwise, costs offulfilling
a contract, which are not capitalized as inventory, property and equipment or intangible assets, are
expensedasincurred.
Contractassetsandcontractliabilities
Acontractassetisrecognizedwhenwerecognizerevenuebeforebeingunconditionallyentitled
to the consideration under the terms in the contract. Contract assets are assessed for ECLs and are
reclassifiedtoreceivableswhentherighttotheconsiderationbecomesunconditional.
A contract liability is recognized when the customer pays non-refundable consideration before
we recognize the related revenue. A contract liability is also recognized if we have an unconditional

right to receive non-refundable consideration before the Group recognizes the related revenue. In such
cases,acorrespondingreceivablewouldalsoberecognized.
When the contract includes a significant financing component, the contract balance includes
interestaccruedundertheeffectiveinterestmethod.
Tradeandotherreceivables
A receivable is recognized when we have an unconditional right to receive consideration and
onlythepassageoftimeisrequiredbeforepaymentofthatconsiderationisdue.
Trade receivables that do not contain a significant financing component are initially measured
at their transaction price. Trade receivables that contain a significant financing component and other
receivables are initially measured at fair value plus transaction costs. All receivables are subsequently
statedatamortizedcost.
Tradeandotherpayables
Tradeandotherpayablesareinitiallyrecognizedatfairvalue.Subsequenttoinitialrecognition,
trade and other payables are stated at amortized cost unless the effect of discounting would be
immaterial,inwhichcasetheyarestatedatinvoiceamounts.
Redemptionliabilities
Acontractthatcontainsanobligationforustopurchase ourownequityinstrumentsforcashor
anotherfinancialassetgivesrisetoafinancialliabilityevenifourobligationtopurchaseisconditional
on the counterparty exercising its right to redeem. The redemption liability is initially measured at the

expensebeingincludedinchangeinthecarryingamountsoffinancialinstrumentsissuedtoinvestors.
Thethencarryingamountoftheredemptionliabilityisreclassifiedtoequityuponatermination
ofthecounterparty’srighttorequestustoredeemourownequityinstruments.
Recognitionofdeferredtaxassets
Deferred tax assets related to deductible temporary differences, tax credits and tax losses are
recognized when management considers it is probable that future taxable profits will be available
againstwhichthedeductibletemporarydifferences,taxcreditsandtaxlossescanbeutilized.Whenthe
expectation is different from the original estimate, such differences will impact the recognition of
deferredtaxassetsandtaxexpensesintheperiodinwhichsuchestimateischanged.
Share-basedpayments
The equity-settled share-based payments granted to employees are measured at grant date fair
value.Theamountisgenerallyrecognizedasanexpense,withacorrespondingincreaseinequity,over
the vesting period of the awards. The amount recognized as an expense is adjusted to reflect the
numberofawardsforwhichtherelatedserviceconditionsareexpectedtobemet,suchthattheamount
ultimately recognized is based on the number of awards that meet the related service conditions at the
